disease_label_per_paper: Acute retroviral syndrome presenting as acute hepatitis
presentation_summary: 25-year-old previously healthy man presented with back pain, headache, diarrhea, and vomiting over two days after feeling ill for three days.
He reported a monogamous relationship with an HIV-positive male partner, regular unprotected anal intercourse, and previous decline of PrEP.

Exam showed fever 38.5 C, heart rate 123/min, blood pressure 130/78 mmHg, moderate distress, normal neuro exam, normal abdominal exam without organomegaly or tenderness, and normal cardiopulmonary exam.
Initial labs showed WBC 3900/uL, hemoglobin 17.6 g/dL, creatinine 1.76 mg/dL, AST 49 U/L, ALT 30 U/L, and total bilirubin 0.31 mg/dL.

The patient continued fever with peak temperature 39.3 C on hospital day 3, and AST/ALT rose to 200/137 U/L on day 2 with INR 1.45 and PTT 62.4 seconds; bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase remained normal.
Evaluation for HAV, HBV, HCV, HEV, HSV, EBV, CMV, autoimmune hepatitis, hemochromatosis, Wilson disease, alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, and liver ultrasound was negative or normal.
Initial fourth-generation HIV antigen-antibody screen was negative, but HIV RNA testing showed >10,000,000 copies/mL, confirming primary HIV infection.
